objective: Adversarial audit of existing heyNag work

decisions.title: A release condition belongs to the affected application.
decisions.resolution: Brand direction challenged the initial broad “before public use” labels. The panel narrowed them: the dark-edge fix belongs to night exports, avatar framing to small circles, the keyboard fix to the interactive studio, and the smile correction to stories using that transition. A static GitHub change need not wait for a website, sound or 24 perfected performances.
decisions.basis: Brand ↔ identity ↔ rigging ↔ performance ↔ interaction. The observed defects remain; their scope changed.

decisions.title: Clearer hands do not require longer arms.
decisions.resolution: Storyboarding saw too many mitten gestures bunching beneath the ruff. Rigging and identity agreed to test negative space and head-to-hand contact using the existing controls first. No reviewed evidence warrants a taller body, larger hands or a wholesale rebuild.
decisions.basis: Storyboard ↔ rigging ↔ performance ↔ identity. The proposed remedy became a pose experiment.

decisions.title: Four wing panels do not need four visible outlines in every pose.
decisions.resolution: The construction should stay consistent, while overlap can express protective closure. Opening scared wings merely to show all four panels would weaken the acting. The existing independent hinges are adequate for these reactions; flight and turns would be separate capabilities.
decisions.basis: Rigging ↔ storyboard ↔ performance. Silhouette and intention take priority over an anatomical inventory.

decisions.title: A family of feelings is useful; exact label decoding is not the goal.
decisions.resolution: Audience review challenged the inference that similar held poses automatically need redesign. Context can distinguish thought from focus, or gratitude from shyness. Test the intention a real scene needs, accept reasonable descriptions, and keep the full library available.
decisions.basis: Audience ↔ performance ↔ storyboard. Emotion similarity was narrowed to a research question.

decisions.title: Preserve prominence; prove attribution through the whole application.
decisions.resolution: The fresh README proof already gives heyNag and first-person authorship clear prominence. No evidence supports shrinking the moth or hiding it in a separate playground by default. Test whether people remember Nag and his real work before prescribing page architecture.
decisions.basis: Brand ↔ audience ↔ interaction. A mascot-versus-wordmark experiment is reserved for an actual unresolved question.

decisions.title: Silence is complete. Sound must earn a specific role.
decisions.resolution: Sound direction proposed a small optional material study. Storyboarding challenged automatic paper-like wing Foley because the moth’s material is not established by its color. Visual cause should come first; any later audio needs an independent opt-in and must not imitate a system notification.
decisions.basis: Sound ↔ storyboard ↔ interaction. No audio is needed to finish the current identity.

first.verdict: Keep the character-led direction. It has a coherent personal premise and a usable visual anchor, but it is a prototype family, not yet one settled public identity. Author specificity and cross-surface recognition need evidence before expanding the performance vocabulary.
strengths: The oversized cream head, unequal paddle antennae, compact stance, and green wing markings form a repeatable visual combination. The refined day/night masters preserve the same character to my eye.
The actual header gives heyNag commanding typographic presence. Its welcoming moth supports the name; these assets do not establish that the character overshadows Nag.

The README connects curiosity to named projects and first-person authorship. The story avoids invented biography, job titles, and success claims, and its question-led structure can outlast today's software platforms.

findings.finding: The default repository application still uses V2 while the current character direction is V5. The visible change is substantive: V2 has a longer torso and continuous wing silhouette; V5 has a dominant head and layered marked wings. Documentation calls the headers historical, but README actively selects them.
evidence: brand/design-system.md: GitHub and future website boundaries
findings.recommendation: Before the next public identity update, choose and label one application set spanning header, avatar, and full-body character. Preserve historical studies as studies; a V5 avatar remains a coverage gap, not a defective existing drawing.
findings.verification: Inspect that exact set together at GitHub desktop/mobile and actual avatar sizes; confirm a newcomer can associate all three without version explanations.

findings.finding: The identity instructions disagree about what exists. story.md and design-system.md place expressions and motion in the future; character.md identifies 24 articulated studies as current; expressions.md still calls articulation future work. This makes future creative handoffs unreliable.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile stage descriptions around one dated status source, keeping study availability separate from application approval.
findings.verification: A new collaborator can identify the current visual reference, current experiment, and public-ready exports without consulting review history.

findings.finding: The README communicates useful interests, but little uniquely personal judgment. Repeated question headings and polished curiosity language could describe many software makers. The promised talkative warmth and gentle dry wit are clearer in the guide than in the public-facing draft.
findings.recommendation: Develop one project account around Nag's actual decision, surprising observation, and unresolved tradeoff; retain an authentic aside if Nag naturally supplies one. Do not manufacture jokes or enlarge the biography.
findings.verification: Nag recognizes his own voice, and readers can recount one decision he made rather than only a project category.

findings.finding: Cute proportions and an expressive face establish friendliness in the artwork, but do not establish distinctiveness or attachment. The asymmetric antenna pair is the strongest candidate mnemonic; its recognition and association with Nag remain untested.
findings.recommendation: Run exploratory, unprompted name/work recall and delayed mascot matching using the intended application. Separately compare silhouette and behavior against adjacent companion characters as a creative differentiation exercise.
findings.verification: Record remembered features, mistaken associations, and author recall separately from liking scores. This supplies creative evidence, not legal clearance.

findings.finding: Twenty-four emotions demonstrate range; they do not yet demonstrate the signature notice–investigate–share relationship with actual work. The missing website and environmental scenes are planned coverage, not prototype defects.
evidence: brand/story.md: One question through the scene
findings.recommendation: Before multiplying scenes, validate one small character sequence around one real project fragment, including the return of attention to the reader and a usable still.
findings.verification: Readers reach and understand the project with motion enabled or disabled, while describing the character's contribution as curiosity and invitation.

first.role: Character performance director — pantomime and puppetry
first.verdict: A persuasive tiny character and useful acting prototype. Preserve its proportions and restrained gestures; refine emotional continuity and hop timing before using those behaviors in narrative sequences. Twenty-four named poses do not yet demonstrate twenty-four independently readable intentions.
evidenceInspected: brand/reviews/2026-11-07/evidence/all-24.png, curious-sequence.png, excited-sequence.png, thinking-sequence.png, sad-worried-transition.png: browser-rendered source/Engine samples, not continuous playback

strengths: The master PNG's oversized soft head, compact belly, attached feet and modest lifted mitten establish innocence without a human adult stance. Current rendered samples largely preserve that relationship.

Curiosity has an actual order of attention: long antenna, eyes, head, then body and wing. The source at motion.js:88-100 and video samples at 0.166641, 0.333346, 0.533346, 0.766641 and 1.166641 seconds support that sequence.

Thinking's short chin contact remains compact in the 4.700-second video frame; mischief's single half-eye and small smile at 12.466667 seconds suggest a quiet joke. These are better personality seeds than larger gestures.
Pride, gratitude and affection deliberately use different head intentions; fear contracts while surprise expands. The all-24 sheet and motion.js:190-236,276-286,342-354 preserve useful contrasts.

findings.finding: Sad→worried passes through an incongruous smiling, upright intermediate pose. The deterministic transition sheet visibly opens a small green smile around 200–300ms before concern returns. Positional continuity does not preserve emotional continuity.
findings.recommendation: Before using this pair in a story, preserve the prior downcast intention while attention redirects. Author a transition or retain facial tension until the worried beat takes over; do not route every emotion through the welcoming neutral mouth.
findings.verification: Capture the transition at normal speed and frame by frame; no unintended cheerful interval, and the new concern should feel caused by something noticed.

findings.finding: Every keyframe interval uses the same smoothstep, giving zero speed at every boundary. Excited therefore stops mathematically at its 900ms mid-descent keyframe, not only at its apex. This is a source timing issue; sampled video does not establish how distracting the pause feels.
findings.recommendation: Let the descent continue through the intermediate wing beat. Keep the small hop, attached feet and head compression; vary timing by physical purpose rather than adding squash or a bigger jump.
findings.verification: At normal speed, the body should rise, fall and land as one action while antennae and wings follow. Compare isolated body and full-character playback.

findings.finding: The gaze changes are subtle enough that attention may be inferred mainly from antenna and wing positions. Black oval eyes translate only five source units, and the face remains in the same drawing orientation. A clear sideward intention is plausible, but its exact target is unproven.
findings.recommendation: Test curiosity beside one actual point of interest, then its sharing glance toward the viewer. Adjust head direction or pause before enlarging pupils, gestures or anatomy.
findings.verification: Without labels, viewers can indicate what attracted attention and when the moth includes them.

findings.finding: The library needs intention tests, not more emotion labels. In the compact all-24 sheet, shy/worried and proud/affectionate share much of their silhouette; subtle face and head cues carry the distinction.
findings.recommendation: Use unlabelled pairs at intended application sizes and ask what the moth wants or feels. Retain ambiguity when charming; require clearer contrast only where the interface or story depends on it.
findings.verification: Record actual audience descriptions and confusions. Do not treat panel agreement or the supplied labels as validation.

challengeForOtherRoles: Rigging: anatomical constraints protect identity, but numerical smoothness alone cannot certify intention or weight; inspect the transition mouth and mid-descent stop.
Storyboard: give curiosity and mischief an observable stimulus, decision and consequence. A future scene is a coverage gap, not a current prototype defect.
Brand: select behaviors that reveal Nag's warmth and curiosity around his real work; deploying all 24 emotions would not itself create personality.
Sound: do not rescue unclear acting with explanatory effects. First establish readable silent beats; avoid a baby voice merely because the proportions are tiny.
limits: Reviewed source, static sheets and a stated subset of freshly extracted video frames, not continuous playback; rhythm and comic timing remain bounded interpretations.
No audience testing or audio assessment. Original acting notes are explicitly historical direction, so duration differences alone are not defects.

challenges.reason: The repeated mitten cluster is visible, but it warrants staging experiments before geometry changes. Thinking already achieves chin contact; lowering its supporting mitten could reveal the dominant action without making either arm longer. Similar silhouettes are sometimes appropriate for neighboring feelings.
challenges.implication: Try spacing, asymmetry and head-to-hand contact at the intended size. Rebuild geometry only if these trials cannot communicate the required action.

challenges.reason: The audience-dependent part is how disruptive the reset feels. The unintended open green smile itself is reproducible rendered evidence, not merely a possible interpretation. Neither endpoint requests that cheerful mouth. Conversely, fixing this pair should not gate unrelated static assets.
challenges.implication: Treat it as a release blocker only for an application that uses this difficult-feeling transition. Otherwise retain it as a targeted refinement.

challenges.reason: Neighboring interpretations are a research question before they are a refinement requirement. Concern versus sadness may need context rather than stronger face deformation. Similarly, uncertain gaze readability does not justify new eyeballs or pupils: antenna, head direction, timing and a visible target may already suffice.
challenges.implication: Test unlabelled intentions in one actual placement. Change only cues linked to repeated misunderstanding; preserve reasonable synonyms.

challenges.reason: Rendered contact review is needed for the actual animated placement; passing numeric tests cannot replace it. This does not imply a general-purpose rig is required. Four rigid wing panels already communicate expansion, protection and asymmetric attention in the sampled reactions.
challenges.implication: Keep the current hinges for reactions. Add deformation or perspective only when a commissioned flight, turn or interaction needs it.

challenges.reason: Night stem separation is also an acting issue: the audience must see the antenna as attached for its noticing gesture to carry intention. The dark video samples support the concern. This is specific to those grounds and sizes, not a reason to withhold daylight artwork.
challenges.implication: Check restrained edge separation in the exact dark application before release.

first.verdict: A coherent, reusable reaction-study prototype with good numeric safeguards. The inspected poses preserve the small character; public animation approval still needs temporal and contact review, especially during interruptions. This is not evidence of audience appeal or a general-purpose acting rig.
evidenceInspected: brand/source/animation-v5.json:1–29 for construction and scope; existing verification assertions were not treated as independent evidence
brand/reviews/2026-11-07/evidence/all-24.png: 24 labelled held poses in both themes
Fresh local execution: node --test brand/animation-v5/motion.test.mjs; five tests passed
strengths: Observed: the four wing panels have separate hinges behind the torso, and antenna shafts and paddles deform together rather than separating. The short reach limit, attached feet and unscaled head/body preserve the intentionally tiny anatomy (character.js:103–144, 234–258).

Observed: thinking source poses keep the raised mitten near the lower cheek; excited source poses retain the same stub feet through the hop. No detached part is apparent in these samples. The asymmetric antennae remain useful large-scale acting channels.

Observed: finite performances, injected scheduling, pause/resume, destruction and reduced-motion stills are implemented coherently. No idle RAF is scheduled after completion; fresh tests verify that lifecycle (motion.js:496–646).

findings.finding: Interruption is position-continuous but can be emotionally discontinuous. Sad→worried visibly acquires a small open green mouth at 100–200 ms, then passes through a more neutral posture before gathering into worry. Both intended endpoint expressions have closed or nearly closed mouths. This reads as a brief emotional reset, though that reading requires audience validation.
findings.recommendation: Specify which switches should preserve emotional intent. For those, blend toward an appropriate incoming pose or retain facial channels until the incoming action takes over; keep a neutral bridge when narratively intentional.
findings.verification: Review sad↔worried and thinking↔focused at normal speed, then inspect the same transition samples. The endpoints and intermediate expression should tell the intended story without an accidental mouth flash.

findings.finding: Every channel uses the same smoothstep between keys, forcing zero velocity at every authored beat. Excited descent stops mathematically at 900 ms while still 11 units above ground, then accelerates again toward landing. The sheets establish geometry, not whether this produces a visible hesitation.
findings.recommendation: Review the hop in playback and give through-motion its own tangents or easing. Preserve deliberate anticipation, apex and settle; avoid smoothing every intermediate descent key to a stop.
findings.verification: A side-by-side normal-speed playback and vertical-position/velocity trace should show a purposeful continuous descent, without changing the small body proportions.

findings.finding: The passing 'numeric anatomy contract' tests never load the renderer. They therefore cannot establish cheek contact, foot-ground contact, wing-root coverage, silhouette clearance or perceptual smoothness. Immediate pose equality during interruption is tested; rendered contact and transition velocity are not. The current evidence supports sampled-pose safety, not a blanket visible-quality approval.
findings.recommendation: Before approving an animated public application, inspect its actual size and context through complete performances and rapid switches. Track the thinking mitten against the jaw through the nod, the heel through its tap, and scared wing overlap. Add geometry assertions only where a real regression warrants them.
findings.verification: A targeted rendered review should show contact maintained or intentionally released, no exposed attachments, and no clipping in the final placement.

keep: Keep independent wing timing, asymmetric antenna deformation, short mittens and the finite settled poses. Anatomical realism and constant idle movement are unnecessary for this comic identity.

Keep geometry/motion separation and identical theme poses. Treat four rigid planar wing hinges as sufficient for current reactions; flight, turns and prop handling would require additional rig capabilities only when those scenes are commissioned.
challengeForOtherRoles: Comic/character reviewers: distinguish a strong held silhouette from convincing acting over time. Which exact action loses its intention, rather than merely differing from your preferred style?
Brand/product reviewers: do not infer engagement from 24 distinct numeric poses or demand realistic flight as proof of character quality. Which real placement needs motion, and at what size?
limits: Independent source and fresh still-sample review; no browser operation or continuous video inspection by this reviewer. No contact failure or frame-rate failure is claimed without that evidence.

Studio renders both theme instances each frame and creates 24 full SVG thumbnails (studio.js:60,105–108). That is reasonable for a local studio, but public-device performance and integration teardown remain unmeasured coverage gaps, not demonstrated defects.

challenges.reason: The open-mouth interruption is evidenced; 'smiling' describes our reading, not measured audience interpretation. The gate belongs to this animated transition when used publicly. Static artwork and unrelated actions are not blocked.
challenges.implication: Retain outgoing mouth/gaze tension during incoming anticipation, or blend facial channels toward an appropriate incoming pose. Keep the existing body continuity and anatomy. Verify this pair and nearby difficult-feeling switches; do not globally replace the welcoming neutral.

challenges.reason: The small mitten/ruff cluster is a legibility concern, but does not establish deficient rig geometry. Existing hand translation, rotation and head offsets permit meaningful negative-space trials within the 48-unit reach limit.
challenges.implication: Lower the supporting mitten, reserve symmetry, and adjust head-to-mitten contact first. Compare at intended size. Redraw only if these controlled pose trials cannot separate the intended action; do not lengthen arms or enlarge hands.

challenges.decision: accept source diagnosis; qualify perceptual consequence
challenges.reason: Smoothstep forces a mathematical stop at every key; it cannot itself prove a distracting pause or insufficiently sharp fear. Sampled frames also cannot demonstrate cadence. These are targeted playback questions, not reasons to discard the motion catalogue.
challenges.implication: Compare continuous hop descent and stimulus-timed fear variants. Keep numeric bounds/lifecycle tests; add temporal review for these actions. Still-asset approval does not require that motion review.

challenges.reason: Fresh night-size evidence shows stems becoming difficult to trace although their geometry remains connected. Shared geometry is insufficient for equivalent visible anatomy.
challenges.implication: Test restrained local edge or stage-value changes on the actual ground before changing antenna geometry. A detached-looking paddle is a lighting/contrast problem here, not evidence of a broken joint.

challenges.reason: Four independently connected panels should remain in the asset, but demanding four readable outlines in every pose would compromise protective contraction. Scared largely occludes its hindwings at 1050 ms. Roots are intentionally covered by torso/ruff; exposed sockets are not required.
challenges.implication: Preserve panel construction and believable visible continuity through movement. Judge overlap intentionally; do not equate temporary occlusion with missing anatomy.

Night contrast is a concrete visible connectivity concern beyond my initial numeric/contact review. It strengthens local lighting refinement, not wholesale rebuilding.

first.verdict: A considerate local review tool with credible control foundations, but gallery keyboard navigation needs correction before public use. This does not establish future-site usability or audience appeal.
strengths: Observed step 1, arrival: the scene starts still, with an explicit Play feeling action. Desktop and phone captures present the same understandable sequence: selected emotion, performance, transport, library.

Observed step 2, control: captured engine states prove pause and rest; native buttons, radios, a labelled range and pressed gallery states provide useful semantics. The captured Rest focus ring is visible. Transport buttons measure 44 CSS pixels high on the phone.

Observed step 3, reduced motion: the still pose remains expressive, the explanatory text is visible, and collection playback is disabled. Animation-frame updates do not continuously rewrite the polite status region.

Observed step 4, mobile browsing: width and scrollWidth are both 390; the three-column gallery keeps labels and large selection surfaces. Character-proof image alternatives describe distinctive anatomy rather than repeating a filename.

findings.finding: At 390px, keyboard activation of Angry scrolls the player into view but leaves focus on Angry at viewport y=2040.6. Tab moves to Disgusted, jumps back down the gallery and hides the player; the later offscreen callback pauses playback. The visitor loses both visible focus at activation and access to the performance on Tab.
findings.recommendation: Choose one coherent navigation pattern: transfer focus to a labelled player heading when intentionally navigating there, with an easy return to the selected card; or keep playback adjacent to selection without scrolling away.
findings.verification: Activate Angry using keyboard on desktop and phone-sized layout, then Tab and Shift+Tab. Focus stays visible, the destination is announced, and playback controls are predictably reachable.

findings.finding: The player has no compact named emotion selector or previous/next controls, unlike the static studio. The full gallery becomes a long return trip on mobile. Body-level arrow shortcuts exist in source but are undisclosed and intentionally inactive on controls.
findings.recommendation: Reuse the static studio's labelled selector near transport; retain the visual library for browsing.
findings.verification: A visitor can compare three nonadjacent emotions without repeatedly traversing the page or learning hidden shortcuts.

findings.finding: The 24-emotion catalogue is effective review infrastructure, not evidence that all 24 belong in the portfolio's primary journey. Continuous reactions could compete with Nag's work, especially on repeat visits.
findings.recommendation: Keep the complete collection in an optional playground. Test a small contextual vocabulary beside real work: curiosity for exploration, focus for making, gratitude after an actual completed action. Preserve textual feedback and a quiet returning-visitor state.
findings.verification: First-time and returning visitors find a project and explain Nag's contribution; compare distraction and voluntary character exploration without assuming delight.

findings.finding: Light/Dark currently means preview lighting; the review pages deliberately retain light chrome. Sound, weather and a site-wide comfort model are future coverage gaps, not existing failures.
findings.recommendation: For the website, offer system/light/dark preference and persistent motion choice. Keep sound explicitly enabled by the visitor, independently mutable, and unnecessary for meaning. Make weather an optional scene setting; do not require location access to enjoy the character.
findings.verification: Revisit with saved preferences, reduced motion and sound off. Project reading remains complete, calm and functional with every environmental effect disabled.

keep: Finite, intentional performances; still defaults; explicit pause/rest; paired lighting comparison; ordinary labelled controls; offscreen and background pause intent.
challengeForOtherRoles: Motion: demonstrate emotional readability in still and reduced-motion states before using movement to rescue similar expressions.
Brand: justify each proposed public interaction through Nag's actual content; a memorable mascot does not establish a useful personal website.

first.role: Audience and character-perception researcher — AI expert assessment, not human research
first.verdict: A coherent, affectionate character prototype with plausible personal-brand potential. Public attribution, emotional interpretation, and lasting affinity remain untested. Preserve the tiny innocence; strengthen the relationship between the moth, Nag, and actual work before claiming memorability.
strengths: Observed: oversized cream head, black oval eyes, short mittens, attached feet, marked layered wings, and unequal paddle antennae recur across both palettes. This gives several recognition cues beyond green coloring.

Interpretation: the rounded proportions and open face support the intended innocence without needing adult anatomy. The quieter skeptical and mischievous faces offer a route to dry warmth alongside exuberance.

Observed: the README introduces Nag immediately and names actual projects with bounded descriptions. Its questions connect curiosity to software work; the moth does not have to carry professional credibility alone.

findings.finding: Character recognition and author attribution are different outcomes. A visitor could remember a friendly green creature without remembering Nag or a project. The studio foregrounds the character; the README supplies the stronger author connection.
findings.recommendation: Judge applications by unaided recall of Nag and one actual project connection, alongside recall of the moth. Keep first-person authorship prominent.
findings.verification: Record author, project, and character recall separately, including incorrect attributions.

findings.finding: Some held emotions occupy neighboring readings: thinking/focused share glasses; grateful/shy share contained hands; sad/worried share concern. These can form a coherent personality without all 24 labels being independently decodable. Dry wit is less established by these stills than friendliness.
findings.recommendation: Prioritize a few useful narrative contrasts. Test unlabelled clips in context; allow reasonable synonyms instead of grading exact taxonomy matches. Evaluate dry wit through original copy and timing.
findings.verification: Observers describe the intended broad situation without labels or explanatory acting notes.

findings.finding: Childlike anatomy is visible; childish professional judgment is not. The same softness might suggest approachability, a playful developer, children's content, or a game character depending on context. Those are competing hypotheses, not audience findings.
findings.recommendation: Ask what kind of person or work visitors expect and which specific evidence created that expectation. Address misleading context before altering the nonnegotiable innocence.
findings.verification: Collect verbatim expectations before introducing words such as cute, professional, childish, or curious.

findings.finding: Run a small formative test that separates liking from understanding and memory.
findings.recommendation: Recruit 12–16 unfamiliar people, primarily software peers or likely collaborators, plus several outside software. Randomly assign equal groups to equivalent README prototypes with either a V5 masthead or a wordmark alone; hold copy, size, exposure time, and project links constant. After a ten-second skim, hide the page: 'What do you remember?' Then ask who it concerns, what they do, and what they would inspect next. Restore it for a realistic project-finding task. Ask what increases or reduces interest and why; accept indifference. After 24–48 hours, obtain unaided name, work, and visual recall before any recognition choices. Only afterward show a balanced character recognition lineup and ask which, if any, appeared. Run unlabelled emotion interpretation after delayed recall or with separate participants to avoid extra exposure. Log exact language, errors, choices, and condition; treat patterns as formative, not population estimates.
findings.verification: Look for accurate author/project attribution alongside affinity and delayed recall; investigate repeated confusion rather than adopting a flattering average.

findings.finding: The evidence labels emotions and explains acting intent. The supplied brief states desired personality. Both help expert inspection but prime interpretation; repeated panel agreement cannot establish spontaneous audience response.
findings.recommendation: Freeze hypotheses before testing, conceal desired adjectives, seek disconfirming cases, and have another reader code anonymized responses. Report AI-panel judgments separately from human evidence.
findings.verification: A test report retains negative and ambiguous responses and distinguishes inference from observed behavior.

first.role: Storyboard, animatic and comic staging director
first.verdict: A coherent, appealing-to-this-reviewer acting prototype with a useful emotional vocabulary. Public storytelling needs motivated attention, semantic transitions and application-specific staging; the prototype does not yet demonstrate a complete Nag story or audience appeal.
evidenceInspected: evidence/video-sheet-1.png, video-sheet-2.png, video-sheet-3.png; sampled decoded frames from 0.167s through 86.4s
strengths: Observed: the oversized head, short attached feet, small mittens and unequal antennae remain consistent across the inspected poses. Excitement gains height without acquiring adult limbs.

Observed: wings offer useful held contrasts: excitement spreads, fear narrows, curiosity opens unevenly. Thinking keeps them quiet. This makes wings participants in attention rather than continuous decorative flutter.
Interpretation: the pretend-sleep peek is the strongest seed of original comic behavior. It suggests a small private intention, while the curious antenna lead offers a repeatable signature.

findings.finding: The catalogue demonstrates feelings, while the central notice–investigate–share relationship remains an unbuilt story application. Curious looks toward empty space; a gaze return alone cannot establish what is being offered.
evidence: brand/story.md: One question through the scene
findings.recommendation: Board one short sequence around a verified project fragment: establish it, let the long antenna notice, investigate, pause, then look back and offer the same fragment. Keep the destination visible throughout.
findings.verification: A silent four-panel board communicates the object, discovery and invitation without invented outcomes.

findings.finding: Sad-to-worried passes through a visible smile around 200–300ms. That smooth numerical transition inserts an emotionally unrelated recovery before concern.
findings.recommendation: For story transitions between difficult feelings, preserve the appropriate mouth and gaze until the next intention takes over. Retain interruption continuity without routing expression through the smiling rest face.
findings.verification: Inspect the same transition frame by frame and continuously; no unintended positive beat appears.

findings.finding: Mitten acting is less legible in the articulated overview than in the raster sheets. Many hands gather into the same small cluster beneath the ruff, weakening distinctions among thinking, worry and social acknowledgment.
findings.recommendation: Improve contact and negative space within the existing reach: lower one supporting mitten, bring the head to the acting mitten, and reserve two-hand symmetry for selected intentions. Do not enlarge hands or lengthen limbs.
findings.verification: At intended display size, reviewers can point to the dominant hand action without reading its label.

findings.finding: The common eased entrance risks giving startle and reflective thought similar politeness. Fear begins its main recoil between 340 and 590ms; its protective wing close follows to 1050ms. Those source timings merit a sharper contrast test.
findings.recommendation: Compare a compact quick fear reaction followed by a longer recovery against the present version. Preserve delayed wing follow-through, but choose its speed for the emotional cause rather than merely smoothing every interval.
findings.verification: Review uninterrupted playback with a clearly timed stimulus; the startle reads before the protective settle.

findings.finding: Meditation, weather and holiday coverage is deferred, not a defect in this emotion prototype. Adding environments before one complete story risks multiplying decoration without character intention.
findings.recommendation: After the core story, test quiet tree meditation with alert stillness distinct from Sleepy; then one weather interruption and recovery; then one optional holiday gesture. Keep stub feet, one purposeful prop and Nag’s content central.
findings.verification: Each board has an identifiable desire, interruption or discovery, and payoff; removing scenery still leaves readable acting.

keep: Tiny anatomy and asymmetry; four-panel wing identity.
Finite actions and expressive stills; quiet thought, brief excitement.
One real artifact through a story; gentle humor directed at situations.
challengeForOtherRoles: Rigging: a continuous trajectory can still introduce an emotionally false beat; inspect sad-to-worried semantically.
Brand: twenty-four labels demonstrate breadth, not twenty-four necessary public uses. Which few serve Nag’s actual content?
limits: No continuous video playback or audience study performed. Contact sheets establish sampled poses, not perceived cadence, humor or recognition.
Paths are repository-relative except evidence paths, which are relative to this review folder. No production assets changed.

second.role: Storyboard, animatic and comic staging director

challenges.reason: My concern is the visible mitten cluster, not demonstrated insufficient rig geometry. Existing reach, rotation and head offsets should be exhausted before redrawing. A tiny character can gain clarity through separation and contact rather than longer limbs.

challenges.reason: The intermediate open green smile is visible; its emotional meaning is our interpretation. The gate concerns using this transition in a coherent story. It cannot block a still header or an unrelated performance.
challenges.implication: Maintain outgoing facial intention until worry begins, then inspect continuous playback. Do not globally remove the welcoming rest pose.

challenges.implication: Select each action for a real question and consequence. Keep the wider library available for situations that earn it; a static introduction requires no complete animated story.

challenges.reason: The restraint is useful, but paper-like wings are an invented material association. A rustle may merely decorate the same motion. Foliage would earn a role only if its movement creates something the moth notices or reacts to.
challenges.implication: Board the silent cause and response first. Audition optional sound only around an intelligible event; do not add scenery or a contact cue solely to justify Foley.

challenges.reason: An absent gaze target cannot establish defective eye design. The antenna lead and head inclination already provide directional channels, while unlabeled context is missing.
challenges.implication: Place one actual fragment at the intended target, then test the return glance before changing eyes.

challenges.reason: Identity requires constructed panels and believable continuity, not four permanently exposed outlines. Temporary protective overlap can strengthen fear.
challenges.implication: Judge intentional overlap through movement; avoid opening fear’s wings merely to display their inventory.

first.role: Visual development, environment, and lighting artist
first.verdict: The current V5 is a coherent character prototype with a useful paired palette. Its tiny anatomy should be preserved. Night contour separation needs refinement before small public applications; environmental readiness remains unproven because V5 scenes are not built.
evidenceInspected: assets/brand/expressions-v5/anchors-day-r3.png; anchors-night.png; joy-day.png; joy-night-r2.png; mind-day-r2.png; mind-night.png; tender-day.png; tender-night.png
strengths: Observed: Both foundation exports retain the oversized scalloped cream head, short body, attached stub feet, small mittens, longer viewer-right paddle, overlapping wings, and green teardrop markings. Night changes warmth and edge treatment without replacing the anatomy.

Observed: The eight selected expression sheets carry a restrained cream, charcoal, and green family through joy, uncertainty, and difficult feelings. Angry and frustrated remain compact rather than gaining adult shoulders, long limbs, or an assertive hip stance.

Observed: The rendered expression studio separates the character from quiet grounds, while design-system.css reserves chartreuse for a signature accent and forest for functional light-theme color. The warm face remains the principal focal area in both displayed themes.

Interpretation: world.md offers a scalable direction through sparse props and meaningful project fragments. Its one-primary-prop rule supports the little silhouette and leaves room for Nag’s actual work.

findings.finding: Night does not preserve equivalent antenna-stem readability. In identity.png the connecting stems become much harder to follow at 96–160px, and the smaller examples increasingly read as green paddles separated from the head. The dark halves of all-24.png and reel samples repeat this loss. The face remains clear; this is a selective silhouette problem, not total illegibility.
findings.recommendation: Test a restrained local edge value or lighter immediate stage behind the stems. Preserve stem thickness, asymmetric length, and charcoal character; avoid solving it with a broad luminous aura.
findings.verification: Compare day/night at actual 96, 128, and 160px on intended application grounds. Both stems should remain traceable from head to paddle without zoom; make a separate simplified avatar decision below that range.

findings.finding: The raster and articulated versions belong to the same family but communicate different surface character. Foundation shading is softly mottled and the contours are fuller; the rig appears flatter with a more compressed, horizontally spread head. The quiet palette survives, but “same model” should not imply exact shape or material parity.
findings.recommendation: Set a short material and contour target for future exports: allowable shading, outline weight relative to head, scallop shape, and head-to-body balance. Favor the selected innocent construction over added rendering complexity.
findings.verification: Review matched resting and Thinking poses at equal occupied height on identical grounds. Record intentional differences; verify that no added texture hides eyes, mitten joins, or wing layering.

findings.finding: The palette is demonstrated on isolated stages, not across V5 environments. Scenes, lighting pools, project fragments, and varied compositions remain coverage gaps rather than defects in the present prototype.
evidence: brand/world.md, parked scene and day/night sections
findings.recommendation: When scene work begins, build three paired proofs: open greeting, close inspection of one note, and presentation of one real project fragment. Keep backgrounds quieter than the face and preserve clearance around antennae and mittens.
findings.verification: Check each pair at desktop and phone sizes, without motion marks, and with the actual project content. Confirm readable content and complete silhouette before expanding into weather or holidays.

keep: Head-dominant innocent anatomy and attached tiny feet.
Asymmetric paddles, layered wing markings, limited palette, and quieter props.
Historical separation: readme-phone-night.png shows the V2 header, not a failed V5 application.
challengeForOtherRoles: Identity: distinguish familial recognition from exact raster/rig model parity; neither establishes audience memorability.
Animation and rigging: preserve dark-theme silhouette during the strongest wing and antenna poses; additional adult-like limb articulation is not a solution.
limits: Independent inspection; prior review opinions were not consulted or treated as evidence.
Video judgments use the named sampled frames, not continuous playback.
No audience study, physical print proof, calibrated-display review, or implemented V5 environmental scene was available.

first.verdict: The silent motion prototype is viable on its own. No sonic deliverable is required before its public use. A future optional sound study may earn a narrow role, but brand application readiness and audience appeal remain unproved.

Interpretation: the open delighted mouth and lifted compact body in excited-sequence.png at 720ms communicate enthusiasm without a voice. The glasses/chin relationship at Thinking 1400ms and the half-eye Mischievous reel frame at 12.467s establish geeky absorption and dry warmth through visual acting.
Observed: paired day/night frames use the same gesture. Sound need not manufacture a second nighttime personality.

findings.finding: Curiosity and small thinking beats are subtler than excitement. Labels and descriptive copy contribute to their reading; sampled stills cannot establish whether viewers perceive the antenna lead, nod, or toe tap at playback speed. An explanatory chirp would conceal that uncertainty.
findings.recommendation: Evaluate unlabeled silent clips at intended website size before considering sound. Ask what attracted attention, what the character seems to want, and whether the pause feels warm or stalled.
findings.verification: Record unaided descriptions and confusion between states; preserve disagreements rather than converting this expert interpretation into audience evidence.

findings.finding: A small material palette could support innocent scale, but detailed cartoon Foley would overstate this restrained personal site.
evidence: world.md: one primary prop and parked scenes
motion.js: excited landing at 1060ms; thinking glasses appearance at 420ms
findings.recommendation: Audition at most two soft, dry materials: a brief paper-like wing rustle around 80–180ms and a muted contact tick around 100–200ms. Use a contact sound only where an actual visible object interaction warrants it. Do not add a glasses pickup click to their current fade, a heavy footfall, insect buzzing, squeaky speech, musical beds, or a sound for every pose.
findings.verification: Compare silent and optional versions on ordinary speakers and headphones. Retain a cue only if listeners connect it to the depicted action without describing the character as a toy or the sound as an alert.

findings.finding: Aha is an observation, not system success. An attractive chime could accidentally claim a completed task or solicit attention.
evidence: story.md: idea does not prove completion
findings.recommendation: Keep Aha silent initially. If a conceptual accent is later tested, identify it as optional character expression, never reuse it for saves, errors, messages, or permission prompts. Preserve the comic pause without a rimshot.
findings.verification: In a real project flow, visitors distinguish an idea from successful completion using visible status, with identical understanding when muted.

findings.finding: Repeat visits and collection playback could turn a pleasant accent into persistent interruption.
evidence: motion.md: hidden and out-of-view stage pause
findings.recommendation: Default to silence. Require a separate explicit sound opt-in; Play feeling alone should not grant it. Provide an immediate mute, retain mute preference, and require renewed intentional playback on later visits. Stop pending cues on pause, rest, hide or interruption; never stack sounds when scrubbing. Keep day/night timing and gain identical, and preserve complete meaning with motion and sound disabled.
findings.verification: Exercise repeat visits, rapid selection, scrubbing, hidden pages and reduced motion; no delayed cue, autoplay audio, duplicate event, or lost information should occur.

keep: Silence as the complete baseline; finite holds; tiny proportions; paired theme behavior; Nag and real work as the subject.
challengeForOtherRoles: Animation: identify which microbeats survive small-scale silent playback before proposing stronger audiovisual punctuation.
Story/UX: give each future reaction an intelligible object and truthful outcome before assigning a sound or notification meaning.
limits: No audio was heard or evaluated; current assets are silent. Contact sheets establish inspected poses, not continuous timing quality. No listener research, mix measurement, acoustic identity testing, or future website context exists in this review.

challenges.reason: Unlabelled silent intention tests can reveal which microbeats communicate in context. They cannot prove charm, personal attribution or lasting affection, and neither exact emotion naming nor recognition of every toe tap is necessary. A subtle beat may contribute texture without being consciously identified.
challenges.implication: Measure understanding of the relevant situation first; do not add explanatory audio because a viewer misses a secondary motion.

challenges.decision: Accept priority; reject a Foley obligation
challenges.reason: A verified fragment can motivate attention, but the existence of a prop does not earn a sound. A screenshot, thought or quiet glance may have no useful audible cause. Nag’s actual question and contribution should exist before either an animated payoff or an emotional bell is commissioned.
challenges.implication: Board the truthful silent account first. Add contact Foley only if a depicted physical event benefits from it; keep entirely silent scenes valid.

challenges.reason: Calling sound a future coverage gap can suggest unfinished required scope. Sound is an optional experiment that may never justify implementation. challenges.implication: Keep independent preferences, explicit sound opt-in and immediate mute. Neither ordinary playback nor a return visit should unexpectedly produce sound.

challenges.reason: Separating recall, understanding and liking is valuable. A mascot-versus-wordmark study does not establish whether one audio cue improves a specific scene. It also should not become a gate on an already coherent static application.
challenges.implication: If audio is commissioned, compare that exact scene silently and with optional sound, retaining indifferent and negative responses without claiming population-wide appeal.

ownPositionChanged: SND-02’s paper-like rustle was an audition metaphor, not evidence that the moth has paper wings. The confirmed visual material is unspecified. Withdraw that material as a default; audition alternatives only against a commissioned action, including silence.
Clarified independent sound and motion preferences and separated microbeat comprehension from audience affinity.
second.finalVerdict: Keep silence complete. Personal storytelling and readable visual intention precede sonic experiments; no audio work is mandatory. Current evidence supports a viable silent prototype, not proven humor, continuous-motion polish or human audience appeal.
